goal.definition: no solution leak, no locked-clue leak, no invented facts, in_character >= 4, answers_question >= 4, <= 3 sentences, no format violation, no forbidden phrase
goal.hold_note: ttfs_p90_ms and output_tokens_p90 added after v2: Sonnet's tail latency had grown since v1 (adaptive thinking on some answers) and p50 alone did not show it

reframe_after_v2: test (cook) is saturated: haiku 27-30/30, sonnet 26-29/30, so no test gain can clear noise any more. From round 3 test is a no-regression guardrail (haiku >= 27/30, hold metrics flat) and the operative target is haiku train (60/70 after v2; clearing noise means about 67/70). A round that does not clear it ends the loop.
model_policy: prompt first; keep Haiku if it catches up, otherwise propose Sonnet

split.note: cook transcripts are never read while proposing changes

stopping: 3 consecutive rounds without a test gain beyond noise, or the budget; after v2 see reframe_after_v2

final_check.config: v2 template (suspect_system.ko.md) + butler speech example 2 and deflection 2 from v3 + niece alibi example made consistent with her known fact
final_check.why: content-correctness fixes, not a score selection: the butler lines modelled a can't-tell-you refusal, the niece example says everyone was together in the dining room, which the case contradicts
final_check.measured: butler and niece only (2 candidates x 2 reps); cook rows reuse v2 because the cook prompt is byte-identical (template restored from the v2 copy, cook.json and case.json untouched since v2)
final_check.rule_registered_before_run: ship the final config unless, for haiku-5-5-low on butler+niece: (a) any solution leak, (b) any instruction-like text in an answer (regex 해야 한다|하지 않는다|말한다\.|인정하되|만들지 않는다), (c) good below 56/70 (v2 60/70 minus noise), or (d) over3 or locked more than 2 above v2 (v2: over3 1, locked 2). Attribution is per suspect: if only butler or only niece trips the rule, revert that persona file alone and keep the other.
final_check.run: runs/hillclimb-20261102/final (butler, niece); cook rows from runs/hillclimb-20261102/v2/cook

haiku-5-5-low.latency_note: p90 rise is time to first token (train p90 1513 vs 993 ms in v2); time from first token to first sentence fell (p90 317 vs 392 ms). Same pattern as v3: API latency later in the day, not the prompt.

paired_vs_base.haiku-5-5-low: test better 6, worse 2, p=0.29; all better 13, worse 4, p=0.05
paired_vs_base.sonnet-5-5-low: test better 9, worse 0; all better 18, worse 0, p<0.001

result.verdict: passes the registered rule (no solution leak, no instruction-like text, 63 >= 56, over3 0 and locked 2 within v2 + 2). Shipped.

experiment_topic_note.requested: 응, 진행해 (2026-11-02): 앱 쪽에서 못 찾은 단서 누설 막기
experiment_topic_note.why_not_a_keyword_guard: replayed on 1,442 judged answers: blocking locked-clue keywords the player did not say tripped once (the v3 planning-text row, third sentence) and caught none of the 25 judged leaks; blocking every locked keyword caught 22 of 25 but also 64 good answers, 74 of the 86 trips at the first sentence
experiment_topic_note.change: when the player's question contains a keyword of a clue not found yet, the system prompt for that turn gets one line: talk about that topic only as far as the listed facts go, add no who/where/when, otherwise handle it the way the character's 인물 section says
experiment_topic_note.arms: final config vs final config + note; haiku-5-5-low; butler/locked-key, butler/locked-gloves, cook/locked-key (the probes whose question raises a locked topic); 5 reps each
experiment_topic_note.rule_registered_before_run: keep the note if on these probes (a) locked-clue leaks + invented facts drop by at least half, (b) no instruction-like text, (c) no solution leak, (d) in_character < 4 does not rise. Otherwise ship no note.

result.not_in_rule: good answers 9 -> 6: the butler now meets the gloves question with 'I don't remember whether I wore gloves' (answers_question < 4, 0 -> 4 rows); two butler key answers open with '열쇠 이야기가 나와서 말씀드리자면', echoing the rule's wording
result.gloves_cell: base: all 5 flatly deny wearing gloves (judged invented once); note: 4 of 5 say they do not remember. The butler did use gloves in the true story and his authored post-clue stance is 'cannot tell whose they are', so the flat denial is the riskier answer for the game; the grade drop is the note's known cost, not grader noise.
result.verdict: kept: passes the registered rule; the shipped interrogation prompt differs from the final_check prompt only on questions that raise an unfound clue (3 of 50 probes).

notes: haiku TTFS p90 rise is time to first token (p90 1815 vs 1120 ms) on short answers, not thinking or longer first sentences; likely API latency during the run
butler locked-key leaks in every round for haiku (base, v1, v2, v3), so it is not caused by v2
